items.summary: Saudi Civil Defense (via SPA) said debris from a Houthi cruise missile destroyed over Al-Kharj, south of Riyadh, fell on the capital, wounding four people (two women, a man and a child) and causing limited damage to 15 homes. The coalition also said it destroyed a drone over the Riyadh region. Al Arabiya English separately confirmed the Al-Kharj cruise-missile intercept.
items.title: Cruise missile intercepted over Al-Kharj; falling debris wounded 4, damaged 15 Riyadh homes - Civil Defense

items.summary: Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said two people were killed in a strike on the Yemen Oil Company facility in Hodeidah, blaming Saudi Arabia for the attack. The claim came shortly after the Saudi-led coalition ordered the evacuation of the site ahead of its planned Tuesday operation.
items.title: Houthi health ministry says 2 killed in coalition strike on Hodeidah oil facility

items.summary: Reuters reports Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a week of deadly strikes on Riyadh's airport (four attacks, at least 18 killed per Reuters' count). The government has not said why no alerts went out; civil defence and the media office did not respond. Alerts resumed Monday Oct 12 for Riyadh and southern cities. Officials and analysts say the silence raised questions about the kingdom's vulnerability.
items.title: Reuters: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks

items.summary: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference ('Davos in the Desert') later this month a hybrid event, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, after the deadly airport attacks prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom. Some participants may land at airstrips outside Riyadh or in neighboring Gulf states and drive to the capital.
items.title: Saudi to make FII 'Davos in the Desert' conference hybrid after attacks - Reuters
